lead: A wing box or fuselage shell is idealised as booms that carry the direct stress, joined by thin skin. With the booms in place, bending a stringer-stiffened section is the unsymmetrical bending problem solved one boom at a time. Two things make it an exam question: the load is skew (lift and drag together give moments about both axes) and the boom areas are usually unequal, which moves the centroid and makes I<sub>xy</sub> non-zero. Only a few universities teach this as a separate topic.
prereq: You need: the general formula from unsymmetrical bending, the sums of thin-walled section properties, and the shear force and bending moment distribution along a wing (from the chapter on loads on an aircraft).

sections.h3: Boom model and its section properties

blocks.text: Each stringer with its strip of effective skin becomes a boom of area A<sub>i</sub> at (x<sub>i</sub>, y<sub>i</sub>); the skin between booms is taken to carry only shear. Then:

items: Find the boom centroid: x̄ = ΣA<sub>i</sub> x<sub>i</sub>/ΣA<sub>i</sub>, ȳ = ΣA<sub>i</sub> y<sub>i</sub>/ΣA<sub>i</sub>.
Measure every boom from it and sum I<sub>xx</sub> = ΣA<sub>i</sub> y<sub>i</sub>², I<sub>yy</sub> = ΣA<sub>i</sub> x<sub>i</sub>², I<sub>xy</sub> = ΣA<sub>i</sub> x<sub>i</sub> y<sub>i</sub>.
If the layout and the areas are symmetric about at least one centroidal axis, I<sub>xy</sub> = 0. Unequal areas on a rectangular layout break the symmetry and give I<sub>xy</sub> ≠ 0.

blocks.text: A symmetric section with a skew load needs only σ = M<sub>x</sub> y/I<sub>xx</sub> + M<sub>y</sub> x/I<sub>yy</sub>. An unsymmetric section needs the full formula with I<sub>xy</sub>.

sections.h3: Skew loads on a wing and a fuselage

blocks.text: Lift acts upwards and drag acts aft, so a wing section carries moments about both axes. Take z along the span, x aft and y up. Upward lift outboard of a section puts the lower booms in tension, so M<sub>x</sub> is negative in this book's convention; aft drag puts the front booms (negative x) in tension, so M<sub>y</sub> is also negative. For a uniform load w per metre over the outboard length l, the moment at the section is w l²/2. A fuselage under a tail load and inertia is treated the same way, with the booms placed round the shell.

items: Find M<sub>x</sub> and M<sub>y</sub> at the station from the load distribution, with their signs.
Find the boom centroid and I<sub>xx</sub>, I<sub>yy</sub>, I<sub>xy</sub>.
Compute k₁ = (M<sub>y</sub> I<sub>xx</sub> − M<sub>x</sub> I<sub>xy</sub>)/D and k₂ = (M<sub>x</sub> I<sub>yy</sub> − M<sub>y</sub> I<sub>xy</sub>)/D.
Evaluate σ<sub>i</sub> = k₁ x<sub>i</sub> + k₂ y<sub>i</sub> at every boom and check that ΣA<sub>i</sub> σ<sub>i</sub> = 0.

The centroid G lies towards the front, and a dashed neutral axis passes through it at minus 2.7 degrees. A note says that ignoring I x y would give minus 137.5 megapascals at boom 2.

examples.question: A wing box is idealised as four booms at the corners of a 600 mm × 200 mm rectangle: boom 1 (front top) 800 mm², boom 2 (rear top) 400 mm², boom 3 (rear bottom) 400 mm², boom 4 (front bottom) 600 mm². Outboard of the station the wing carries a uniform lift of 3.75 kN/m and a uniform drag of 0.75 kN/m over 4 m. Find the boom stresses, and the error made by ignoring I<sub>xy</sub>.
steps: Moments: lift gives 3.75 × 4²/2 = 30 kN·m, compressing the top booms, so M<sub>x</sub> = −30 kN·m = −3.0 × 10⁷ N·mm. Drag gives 0.75 × 4²/2 = 6 kN·m with the front in tension, so M<sub>y</sub> = −6.0 × 10⁶ N·mm.
I<sub>xx</sub> = ΣA y² = 21,818,182 mm⁴; I<sub>yy</sub> = ΣA x² = 183,272,727 mm⁴; I<sub>xy</sub> = ΣA x y = -4,363,636 mm⁴; D = 3.980 × 10¹⁵ mm⁸.
k₁ = (M<sub>y</sub> I<sub>xx</sub> − M<sub>x</sub> I<sub>xy</sub>)/D = -0.0658 N/mm³; k₂ = (M<sub>x</sub> I<sub>yy</sub> − M<sub>y</sub> I<sub>xy</sub>)/D = -1.3882 N/mm³.
σ<sub>i</sub> = k₁ x<sub>i</sub> + k₂ y<sub>i</sub> at each boom (table).
The neutral axis is at tan⁻¹(−k₁/k₂) = -2.7° to the x axis.
examples.answer: σ₁ = -111.8 MPa, σ₂ = -151.3 MPa, σ₃ = +126.3 MPa, σ₄ = +165.8 MPa. Ignoring I<sub>xy</sub> gives -137.5 MPa at boom 2 instead of -151.3 MPa, an unsafe error of 13.8 MPa on the most compressed boom.

traps: Using the centroid of the box outline instead of the centroid of the boom areas; with unequal booms they differ by tens of millimetres.
Taking I<sub>xy</sub> = 0 because the booms sit on a rectangle. Unequal areas make I<sub>xy</sub> non-zero.
Getting the sign of M<sub>x</sub> or M<sub>y</sub> wrong. Decide which booms the load stretches, then apply the convention.
Skipping the check ΣA<sub>i</sub> σ<sub>i</sub> = 0, which catches most centroid and sign slips.

quiz.q: What does a boom represent in a stringer-stiffened section?
quiz.a: A stringer and its strip of effective skin, lumped as a concentrated area that carries direct stress; the skin between booms carries shear.

quiz.q: Why do unequal boom areas on a rectangular layout give I<sub>xy</sub> ≠ 0?
quiz.a: The centroid moves towards the larger booms, so the booms are no longer at (±a, ±b) about it and the products A x y do not cancel.

quiz.q: Four booms of 100 mm² sit at (±100, ±50) mm. Find I<sub>xx</sub> and I<sub>yy</sub>.
quiz.a: I<sub>xx</sub> = 4 × 100 × 50² = 1,000,000 mm⁴; I<sub>yy</sub> = 4 × 100 × 100² = 4,000,000 mm⁴; I<sub>xy</sub> = 0 by symmetry.

quiz.q: For the worked example, find M<sub>x</sub> at a station 2 m further outboard (outboard length 2 m).
quiz.a: M<sub>x</sub> = −3.75 × 2²/2 = −7.5 kN·m; the moment falls with the square of the outboard length.

quiz.q: In the worked example, why does ignoring I<sub>xy</sub> underestimate the stress at boom 2 but overestimate it at boom 1?
quiz.a: I<sub>xy</sub> is negative, so the extra terms −M<sub>x</sub> I<sub>xy</sub> x/D and −M<sub>y</sub> I<sub>xy</sub> y/D add to the stress at some booms and subtract at others according to the signs of x and y. Boom 2 is aft and up, boom 1 forward and up, so the corrections have opposite signs: −13.8 MPa at boom 2 (−137.5 → −151.3) and +6.0 MPa at boom 1 (−117.9 → −111.8).

quiz.q: Which load input is needed at a wing station before any boom stress can be found?
quiz.a: The bending moments M<sub>x</sub>(z) and M<sub>y</sub>(z) at that station, with signs, from the lift, drag and inertia distributions outboard of it.

beyond: Production wing boxes have twenty or more stringers, and sizing codes run this calculation at every rib station for hundreds of load cases. Finite element models replace the boom idealisation when cut-outs and shear lag matter. Search for "boom idealisation wing box" and "direct stress wing skin stringer".
